config.title: Project Scaffold

intro.title: Project Scaffold
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a basic Angular project scaffold from scratch. You'll learn how to use the Angular CLI to generate the foundational structure of an Angular application. The core concept involves understanding Angular's modular architecture and how components fit together. You'll work with key technologies like TypeScript, Angular modules, and component templates. By the end, you'll have a working Angular application ready for further development.
intro.usecase: Every Angular application starts with a proper project scaffold - from enterprise dashboards like Salesforce's analytics interface to e-commerce platforms like Shopify's admin panel. Developers use the Angular CLI to generate the foundational structure with components, modules, and services organized in a maintainable way. This scaffold ensures consistent architecture across teams, enabling features like user management systems, product catalogs, and real-time data displays to be built efficiently. Setting up the project correctly from the beginning prevents technical debt and makes it easier to add features like authentication flows, API integrations, and responsive layouts later.

objectives: Execute the Angular CLI command to generate a new project with default settings
Apply TypeScript configuration to establish strict type checking for the project
Construct the core application component with proper Angular decorator syntax
Utilize component templates to define the initial HTML structure
Implement component styles to apply basic CSS formatting
Define the application module to declare and bootstrap components
Invoke the development server to compile and serve the application locally
Access the application in a web browser to verify the scaffolded project
Modify the default component template to display custom content
Control project structure by navigating and inspecting generated files and folders
Apply Angular CLI commands to generate additional components within the project
Use the package.json file to manage project dependencies and scripts

steps.title: Import Component decorator from '@angular/core'
steps.instruction: Import the Component decorator from the '@angular/core' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with the Component symbol from '@angular/core'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing Component decorator
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Component decorator is imported and ready to be used for creating Angular components.
successCriteria: The import statement for Component from '@angular/core' is correctly added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Component decorator, which is essential for creating Angular components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement needs to be exactly correct. Make sure you're importing 'Component' from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import Component from '@angular/core' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the AppComponent class
steps.instruction: Create a class named AppComponent that will serve as the root component.
steps.hint: Use the 'class' keyword followed by the class name. You don't need to add any properties or methods yet.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Component decorator from '@angular/core' here

// Create the AppComponent class here
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined, ready to be decorated as a component in the next step.
successCriteria: The code contains a class named 'AppComponent'
The class is defined with the 'class' keyword
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the AppComponent class. This is the foundation of your root component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a class named 'AppComponent' using the 'class' keyword.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent class wasn't created correctly. Remember to use 'class AppComponent {}' syntax.

steps.title: Add the @Component decorator to AppComponent
steps.instruction: Add the @Component decorator above the AppComponent class declaration. Use the imported Component decorator from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Place @Component() directly above the class declaration. The parentheses can be empty for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class now has the @Component decorator applied, which marks it as an Angular component.
successCriteria: The code should have @Component() placed directly above the AppComponent class declaration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the @Component decorator to AppComponent. This decorator is essential for Angular to recognize this class as a component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added @Component() directly above the class declaration, using the imported Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The @Component decorator is missing or incorrectly placed. It should be added directly above the AppComponent class declaration.

steps.title: Configure the component selector
steps.instruction: Add a selector property to the @Component decorator with the value 'app-root'.
steps.hint: Inside the @Component decorator, add a property named selector with the string value 'app-root'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have a selector configured, allowing it to be used in templates as <app-root>.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a selector property with the exact value 'app-root'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully configured the component selector. This allows Angular to recognize <app-root> tags in templates as instances of your AppComponent.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the selector property inside the @Component decorator with the exact value 'app-root'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The selector property is missing or incorrect. Add 'selector: "app-root"' inside the @Component decorator object.

steps.title: Configure the component template
steps.instruction: Add a template property to the @Component decorator with a simple h1 element that says 'Hello Angular!'
steps.hint: Inside the @Component decorator object, add a template property with a string value containing the HTML.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have a basic HTML template defined in its decorator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a template to your component. This defines the HTML structure that will be rendered when the component is used.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've added the template property correctly. Make sure it's inside the @Component decorator object and contains an h1 element with text.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The template property wasn't added correctly. Remember to add 'template: "

Hello Angular!

"' inside the @Component decorator object.

steps.title: Import NgModule from '@angular/core'
steps.instruction: Import the NgModule decorator from '@angular/core' in the same import statement as Component.
steps.hint: Add NgModule to the existing import statement from '@angular/core'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NgModule decorator is imported and available for use in creating the app module.
successCriteria: The import statement includes NgModule from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported NgModule, which is essential for creating Angular modules.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing NgModule from '@angular/core' in the same import statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement doesn't include NgModule from '@angular/core'. Check the syntax and try again.

steps.title: Import BrowserModule from '@angular/platform-browser'
steps.instruction: Add an import statement to bring in BrowserModule from '@angular/platform-browser'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the module name and its source path.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing a module
import { BrowserModule } from '@angular/platform-browser';
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have an import statement for BrowserModule, making it available for use in the application.
successCriteria: The import statement for BrowserModule from '@angular/platform-browser' is correctly added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported BrowserModule, which provides essential browser-specific services and directives for Angular applications.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Check that you're importing BrowserModule from the correct package '@angular/platform-browser'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import for BrowserModule is missing or incorrect. Make sure to import it from '@angular/platform-browser'.

steps.title: Create the AppModule class
steps.instruction: Create a class named AppModule that will serve as the root module.
steps.hint: Use the 'class' keyword followed by the class name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppModule class is created and ready to be decorated with @NgModule.
successCriteria: The code contains a class declaration named AppModule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the AppModule class. This will serve as the root module for your Angular application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a class named AppModule using the 'class' keyword.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppModule class hasn't been created yet. Use the 'class' keyword followed by AppModule to create the class.

steps.title: Add the @NgModule decorator to AppModule
steps.instruction: Add the @NgModule decorator above the AppModule class declaration. The decorator should be imported from '@angular/core' and will be configured in the next steps.
steps.hint: Use the @NgModule decorator with empty parentheses for now. Make sure it's placed directly above the class declaration.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppModule class now has an @NgModule decorator above it, making it a proper Angular module.
successCriteria: The code should have @NgModule({}) placed directly above the AppModule class declaration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the @NgModule decorator to AppModule. This decorator marks the class as an Angular module that will be configured in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added @NgModule({}) directly above the AppModule class declaration. Check that the parentheses are included and the decorator is properly positioned.
steps.feedbackWrong: The @NgModule decorator wasn't added correctly. Remember to place @NgModule({}) directly above the AppModule class declaration. The decorator should be imported from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Declare AppComponent in the module
steps.instruction: Inside the @NgModule decorator, add a 'declarations' array property that contains the AppComponent class.
steps.hint: The declarations array tells Angular which components belong to this module. Add it as a property inside the @NgModule decorator object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent is properly registered in the AppModule through the declarations array.
successCriteria: The @NgModule decorator should have a 'declarations' property with an array containing 'AppComponent'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully declared AppComponent in the module. This tells Angular that AppComponent belongs to this module and can be used in templates.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a 'declarations' array property inside the @NgModule decorator object, and that it contains 'AppComponent'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The module needs a declarations array with AppComponent. Check that you've added the declarations property correctly inside @NgModule({}).

steps.title: Import BrowserModule in the module
steps.instruction: Add an imports array to the @NgModule decorator containing BrowserModule.
steps.hint: The imports array should be added as a property inside the @NgModule decorator object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppModule should now import BrowserModule, which is required for running Angular applications in a browser.
successCriteria: The @NgModule decorator should have an imports property with BrowserModule inside an array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added BrowserModule to the imports array. This module provides essential services for browser applications.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that BrowserModule is inside an array and the property name is 'imports' (not 'import').
steps.feedbackWrong: The @NgModule decorator still needs an imports array containing BrowserModule. Make sure to add it as a property inside the decorator object.

steps.title: Bootstrap AppComponent from the module
steps.instruction: Add a 'bootstrap' array property to the @NgModule decorator configuration object, containing AppComponent as the root component to bootstrap.
steps.hint: The bootstrap property should be an array with AppComponent inside it, similar to how you added the declarations array earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppModule is configured to bootstrap AppComponent as the root component when the application starts.
successCriteria: The @NgModule decorator configuration object includes a 'bootstrap' property with an array containing AppComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added the bootstrap array to the @NgModule decorator. This tells Angular which component to use as the root when the application starts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check the syntax. The bootstrap property should be an array containing AppComponent, similar to the declarations array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The bootstrap configuration is missing or incorrect. Remember to add a 'bootstrap' property to the @NgModule decorator configuration object with AppComponent inside an array.
